explanation: Mixed. The most common strong pattern is the domain-suffix token '.org'/'.com'/'.co' inside URLs, especially 'boost.org' in license headers. It also fires on scattered code tokens (isempty, ' =', 'ee' in pointee, '.Object'), word-piece continuations in names and foreign text ('stein', 'o' in Hippo, Greek 'τ'), and digits in long numbers. Weak firing on ordinary prose words.

Fires on the second or later sub-word piece of a long word that is split into several tokens, mostly medical or scientific terms (transga-str-ic, cere-bro-vascular, gastro-cnemius, vestib-ular, hydro-xylase) and also capitalized pieces (TH-IR-TY, SPI-R-IT, NON-P-RE-CEDENTIAL). The token is a fragment and the word is not finished yet. There are a few odd strong cases (indentation whitespace, ' per', ' of' in 'Battle of').

Fires on tokens inside code and software license or copyright boilerplate: class-name pieces in Objective-C '[[X alloc]' (Asset, J), ' public' and ' using' keywords, and the boilerplate connectors 'free software:', 'name of', 'Inc. and/or its affiliates'. It is a loose code/boilerplate-structure detector. Prose gets only weak firing.

No clear common feature. Activations spread across code-argument tokens (',y' in a macro, 'target', ' >&'), license boilerplate words, legal citation 'al', math variables and ordinary prose nouns ('newspaper', 'facility', 'States', 'chat'). Activation is fairly flat (around 60%) across unrelated contexts.

Fires on the first sub-word piece of a word, often a proper noun or technical term, that will be continued by more pieces: 'py|ro|lytic', 'cy|to|chrome', ' mol|ten', ' s|apphire', ' Ka|unas', ' T|angerang', ' C|iena', 'Mi Granja'. A second job is the 'android:' prefix in XML attributes and short variable names before a method ('e.printStackTrace', 'tz.offset').

Diffuse. Fires on mid-sentence function words and word-starts in German, Chinese and Japanese text ('er|wartete', 'h|arte', 'vor|angegangenen'), on pronouns in phrases like 'what you need' or 'the only thing we want', on the first digit of a number in a range, and on broken multibyte characters. There is no single consistent trigger.

Mostly fires on the final suffix piece that completes a multi-token word or compound ('quadr-ature', 'rocket-prop-elled', 'goal-sc-oring', 'cardiorespir-atory', 'extramar-ital', 'fe-vers', 'six-day', 'multi-family'). It also has scattered strong firing on plain content words in prose ('finer', 'elements', 'historical', 'fever', ' seem').

Low-specificity unit for technical Q&A and code contexts. Its examples include Russian text in programming Q&A, especially sentence-initial word pieces after 'A:' ('Нав', 'Об', 'На'); code tokens (start_link, '::', opencv, URL '&'); and indentation whitespace inside jQuery $.ajax option blocks. Outside such contexts it gives only weak firing.

Fires on words for supplying supporting material or information in a request or bug report: 'screenshots', 'screen shot', 'screenshot', 'error details', 'code sample', 'photos', 'link', 'attached', 'information'. It is strongest for 'add screenshots' in issue templates. It fires moderately on helper verbs in requests ('so we can send you', 'let me know').

Fires on word-initial or mid-word sub-word pieces of longer words that are split into several tokens, often in Romance-language text (French 'ré|duit', Portuguese 'desenv|olvendo', 'des|fazer', accented 'é'/'©') and chemical or medical terms ('-p|yrimethamine', 'metal|lop|olymer', 'cran|ios|ynostosis'). There are some odd English cases ('real world app', ' This').

Fires on the word 'business' or 'Business' (any case, including 'BUSINESS' and pieces of it) in all senses: business days, business interruption in license text, business model, business news. It is near zero elsewhere.

Mixed. Strongest pattern is the argument-opening token right after a function name in math notation ('g(u', 'p(b', 'f(x', 't(', 'j(v'). It also fires on citation labels '[@B', and on various completions of names or words ('Han Solo', 'Ailey', 'kimono', 'right click', '.animate', 'Scanner').

Fires on a token that completes a known multi-token name or identifier, often a CamelCase API or class name in code (UIAlertView, .currentTimeMillis, decodeURIComponent, UITableViewCell, NSIndexPath, .facebook, 'fwlink/?') and also proper names or word endings (Assange, Scorpion, do-able, thermo-ionic). It also fires on broken CJK or Devanagari multibyte pieces.

Fires on markup and citation syntax tokens: HTML entities ('&#'), 'br' inside
tags, the '@' in academic citation keys like '[@CR1]' or '[@B9]', 'pone' in '[@pone...' keys, '@returns' in JSDoc, and LaTeX '\mathfrak'. It fires weakly on the prefix 'sub' and on CSS selectors.
